results.title: Kourovka Problem 18.52 (generation by two elements of prime-power order)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that every finite simple group $G$ is generated by two elements $x, y \in G$ whose orders are prime powers, that is, each of the form $p^k$ with $p$ prime and $k \ge 1$ (the primes and exponents may differ between $x$ and $y$ and depend on the group). The problem is due to J. Krempa.

results.title: Finite simple groups are generated by two elements of prime-power order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every finite simple group $G$ is generated by two elements $x, y \in G$ whose orders are prime powers, that is, each of the form $p^k$ with $p$ prime and $k \ge 1$, where the prime and the exponent may differ between $x$ and $y$. This answers Kourovka Problem 18.52 positively.

results.title: Separated subsets of a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two subsets $A$ and $B$ of a group $G$ are separated, in the sense of I. V. Protasov, when there is an infinite subset $X \subseteq G$ with $1 \in X$, $X^{-1} = X$ and $XAX \cap B = \emptyset$, where $XAX = \{x a y : x, y \in X,\ a \in A\}$.

results.title: Separation of small disjoint subsets of infinite groups (Kourovka 17.102)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement, posed by I. V. Protasov, that for every infinite group $G$ and all disjoint subsets $A, B \subseteq G$ with $|A| < |G|$ and $|B| < |G|$, the sets $A$ and $B$ are separated.

results.title: Small disjoint subsets of an infinite group need not be separated
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist an infinite group $G$ and disjoint subsets $A, B \subseteq G$ with $|A| < |G|$ and $|B| < |G|$ such that $A$ and $B$ are not separated. That is, the statement of Kourovka Problem 17.102 is false.

results.title: The square theta series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The square theta series is the formal power series $\theta(q) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{m^2}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$: for each $n \ge 0$, its coefficient of $q^n$ is the number of integers $m$ with $m^2 = n$.

results.title: Triangular theta series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The triangular theta series is the formal power series $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$ with integer coefficients: for each natural number $n$, its coefficient of $q^n$ is the number of natural numbers $m$ with $m(m+1)/2 = n$.

results.title: First coefficients of the square theta series
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In the square theta series $\theta(q) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{m^2}$, the coefficients of $q^0$, $q^1$, $q^2$ and $q^4$ are $1$, $2$, $0$ and $2$ respectively.

results.title: First coefficients of the triangular theta series
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In the triangular theta series $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$, the coefficients of $q^0$, $q^1$, $q^2$ and $q^3$ are $1$, $1$, $0$ and $1$ respectively.

results.title: The square theta series is a unit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The square theta series $\theta(q) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{m^2}$ is a unit of the ring $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$ of formal power series with integer coefficients, since its constant coefficient is $1$.

results.title: The triangular theta series is a unit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The triangular theta series $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$ is a unit of the ring $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$ of formal power series with integer coefficients, since its constant coefficient is $1$.

results.title: Representation numbers for sums of squares
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an integer $k$ and a natural number $n$, $r_k(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\theta(q)^k$, where $\theta(q) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{m^2}$. Since $\theta$ has constant coefficient $1$, it is a unit of $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$, so $\theta^k$ is a power series for negative $k$ as well.

results.title: Representation numbers for sums of triangular numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an integer $k$ and a natural number $n$, $t_k(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\psi(q)^k$, where $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$. Since $\psi$ has constant coefficient $1$, it is a unit of $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$, so $\psi^k$ is a power series for negative $k$ as well.

results.title: The one-square counts are the coefficients of the square theta series
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an integer $k$ and $n \ge 0$, let $r_k(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\theta(q)^k$, where $\theta$ is the square theta series. Then for every $n \ge 0$, $r_1(n)$ equals the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\theta(q)$.

results.title: Triangular representation numbers with one summand
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an integer $k$, let $t_k(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\psi(q)^k$, where $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$. Then for every natural number $n$, $t_1(n)$ equals the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\psi(q)$.

results.title: Divisibility of square representation counts by a large prime is periodic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an integer $k$ and $n \ge 0$, let $r_k(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\theta(q)^k$, where $\theta$ is the square theta series; for $k \ge 1$ it is the number of representations of $n$ as an ordered sum of $k$ squares of integers. Let $n \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$ be integers and let $p$ be a prime with $p \ge n + 1$. If $p$ divides $r_k(n)$, then $p$ divides $r_{k+jp}(n)$ for every integer $j$.

results.title: Prime divisibility of triangular representation numbers persists under prime shifts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an integer $k$, let $t_k(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\psi(q)^k$, where $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$. Let $n \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$ be natural numbers and let $p$ be a prime with $p \ge n + 1$. If $p$ divides $t_k(n)$, then $p$ divides $t_{k+rp}(n)$ for every integer $r$.

results.title: Window congruence for sums of squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an integer $k$, let $r_k(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\theta(q)^k$, where $\theta(q) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{m^2}$. Let $n \ge 1$, let $p$ be an odd prime with $p - 1 \ge n + 1$, and let $s \ge p$ be an integer. Then $p$ divides $\sum_{i=0}^{p-1} r_{s-i}(n)$.

results.title: Window congruence for sums of triangular numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an integer $k$, let $t_k(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\psi(q)^k$, where $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$. Let $n \ge 1$, let $p$ be an odd prime with $p - 1 \ge n + 1$, and let $s \ge p$ be an integer. Then $p$ divides $\sum_{i=0}^{p-1} t_{s-i}(n)$.

results.title: Representability criterion from a window of counts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an integer $k$ and $n \ge 0$, let $r_k(n)$ and $t_k(n)$ be the coefficients of $q^n$ in $\theta(q)^k$ and $\psi(q)^k$, where $\theta$ and $\psi$ are the square and triangular theta series (units of $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$). Let $n \ge 1$, let $p$ be an odd prime with $p - 1 \ge n + 1$, and let $s$ be an integer. If $p$ does not divide $r_{s-1}(n) + r_{s-2}(n) + \cdots + r_{s-(p-1)}(n)$, then $r_s(n) \ne 0$. Likewise,…

results.title: Window criterion for representability by triangular numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an integer $k$, let $t_k(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\psi(q)^k$, where $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$. Let $n \ge 1$ and let $p$ be an odd prime with $p - 1 \ge n + 1$. For every integer $s$, if $p$ does not divide $\sum_{i=1}^{p-1} t_{s-i}(n)$, then $t_s(n) \ne 0$.

results.title: A prime between $p/2$ and $p$ divides the representation counts of $p$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For integers $k, n \ge 1$, let $r_k(n)$ be the number of representations of $n$ as an ordered sum of $k$ squares of integers and $t_k(n)$ the number of representations of $n$ as an ordered sum of $k$ triangular numbers $m(m+1)/2$ with $m \ge 0$. Let $p$ be an odd prime and $\ell$ a prime with $p/2 < \ell < p$. Then $\ell$ divides both $r_\ell(p)$ and $t_\ell(p)$.

results.title: Logarithmic coefficients of the triangular theta series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $b_n$ be the rational number $b_n = \sum_{d \mid n,\ n/d \text{ odd}} 1/d - \sum_{d \mid n,\ n/d \text{ even}} 1/d$, where $d$ runs over the positive divisors of $n$; for $n = 0$ the sums are taken to be empty, so $b_0 = 0$.

results.title: First logarithmic coefficients of the triangular theta series
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Integer zeros of the sums-of-squares counting polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an integer $k$ and $n \ge 0$, let $r_k(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\theta(q)^k$, where $\theta$ is the square theta series. For every $n \ge 0$ there is a polynomial $P(z) = \sum_i c_i z^i$ with integer coefficients such that $P(z) = n! \, r_z(n)$ for every integer $z$, and every nonzero integer $k$ with $r_k(n) = 0$ divides $c_1$ and satisfies $|k| < 2 |c_i|^{1/(n-i)}$ for some $i$ with $0 \le i < n$.

results.title: Integer roots of triangular representation numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an integer $k$, let $t_k(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\psi(q)^k$, where $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$. For every natural number $n$ there is a polynomial $P(z) = \sum_i a_i z^i$ with integer coefficients such that $P(z) = n!\, t_z(n)$ for every integer $z$, and every nonzero integer $k$ with $t_k(n) = 0$ divides $a_1$ and satisfies $|k| < 2 |a_i|^{1/(n-i)}$ for some $i < n$.

results.title: Hilbert–Waring theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $k \ge 1$ there is a natural number $g$ such that every natural number $n$ is a sum of $g$ $k$-th powers of natural numbers, that is, $n = x_1^k + \dots + x_g^k$ for some $x_1, \dots, x_g \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Legendre's four-triangular-numbers theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $k \ge 0$ let $T_k = k(k+1)/2$ be the $k$-th triangular number. For every natural number $j$, the number of ordered quadruples $(k_1, k_2, k_3, k_4)$ of integers with $0 \le k_i \le j$ and $T_{k_1} + T_{k_2} + T_{k_3} + T_{k_4} = j$ equals $\sigma(2j+1)$, the sum of the positive divisors of $2j+1$.

results.title: Waring's problem for Hurwitz quaternion integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Call a rational quaternion a Hurwitz integer if its four coordinates are either all integers or all of the form $a + \tfrac12$ with $a$ an integer. For every positive integer $\ell$ with $\ell \equiv 1$ or $\ell \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ there is a natural number $g$ such that every Hurwitz integer is a sum of at most $g$ $\ell$-th powers of Hurwitz integers.

results.title: Fourier coefficients of a Fourier monomial on the 2-torus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For frequencies $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the $n$-th Fourier coefficient, taken with respect to normalized Haar measure on $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$, of the monomial $e_m(x) = e^{2\pi i\, m \cdot x}$ is $1$ if $n = m$ and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Integrability of Fourier integrands on the 2-torus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every continuous function $f : (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ and every frequency $n \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the function $x \mapsto e^{-2\pi i\, n \cdot x} f(x)$ is integrable with respect to normalized Haar measure.

results.title: Additivity of Fourier coefficients on the 2-torus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For continuous functions $f, g : (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ and every frequency $n \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the $n$-th Fourier coefficient $\hat h(n) = \int e^{-2\pi i\, n \cdot x} h(x)\,dx$ (normalized Haar measure) satisfies $\widehat{f + g}(n) = \hat f(n) + \hat g(n)$.

results.title: Homogeneity of Fourier coefficients on the 2-torus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $c \in \mathbb{C}$, every continuous function $f : (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ and every frequency $n \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the $n$-th Fourier coefficient (normalized Haar measure) satisfies $\widehat{c f}(n) = c\, \hat f(n)$.

results.title: Axis frequency
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $i \in \{0, 1\}$, the axis frequency $e_i$ is the frequency in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ whose $i$-th coordinate is $1$ and whose other coordinate is $0$.

results.title: Lowest-shell unit polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ let $e_n(y) = e^{2\pi i\, n \cdot y}$ be the Fourier monomial on the unit torus $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$. The lowest-shell unit polynomial is the continuous function $P : (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ given by $P = (4\pi)^{-1}\bigl(e_{(1,0)} + e_{(-1,0)} + e_{(0,1)} + e_{(0,-1)}\bigr)$, the normalized sum of the Fourier monomials of the four nonzero frequencies of smallest…

results.title: Lowest-shell witness
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The lowest-shell witness is the continuous real function $u$ on the torus $(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ given by $u(x_1, x_2) = \frac{1}{4\pi}(e^{i x_1} + e^{-i x_1} + e^{i x_2} + e^{-i x_2}) = \frac{\cos x_1 + \cos x_2}{2\pi}$, the normalized sum of the four lowest nonzero Fourier modes.

results.title: The lowest-shell unit polynomial is real-valued
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every point $y$ of the unit torus $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$, the lowest-shell unit polynomial $P$ satisfies $\operatorname{Im} P(y) = 0$.

results.title: Unit representative of the lowest-shell witness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The unit representative of the lowest-shell witness is the lowest-shell polynomial $(4\pi)^{-1}\bigl(e_{(1,0)} + e_{(-1,0)} + e_{(0,1)} + e_{(0,-1)}\bigr)$ on the unit torus $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$, where $e_n(y) = e^{2\pi i\, n \cdot y}$ for $n \in \mathbb{Z}^2$.

results.title: Lowest frequency shell
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The lowest shell is the set $\{e_1, -e_1, e_2, -e_2\}$ of frequencies in $\mathbb{Z}^2$, where $e_1 = (1, 0)$ and $e_2 = (0, 1)$; these are the four nonzero frequencies of smallest length.

results.title: Fourier coefficients of the lowest-shell witness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every frequency $k \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the Fourier coefficient of the lowest-shell witness at $k$ equals $1/2$ if $k$ lies in the lowest shell, that is, $k$ is one of $(1, 0)$, $(-1, 0)$, $(0, 1)$, $(0, -1)$, and equals $0$ otherwise.

results.title: The lowest-shell witness is in $H^2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The lowest-shell witness $u$ belongs to the spectral Sobolev space $H^2$: if $a_k(u)$ denotes its Fourier coefficients, the series $\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} (1 + |k|^2)^2 |a_k(u)|^2$ converges.

results.title: Gradient energy of the lowest-shell witness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The gradient energy of the lowest-shell witness equals $1$.

results.title: Laplacian energy of the lowest-shell witness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Laplacian energy of the lowest-shell witness equals $1$.

results.title: The lowest-shell witness has mean zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The lowest-shell witness, the function $w(x_1, x_2) = (\cos x_1 + \cos x_2)/(2\pi)$ on the torus $(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$, has mean $0$.

results.title: The unit rescaling fixes the origin
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The coordinate rescaling from the torus $(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ to the unit torus $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$ maps $0$ to $0$.

results.title: Value of the lowest-shell witness at the origin
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The lowest-shell witness $u$ takes the value $u(0) = 1/\pi$ at the origin of the torus.

results.title: The lowest-shell witness is a zero-mean $H^2$ function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The lowest-shell witness $u$ belongs to the spectral Sobolev space $H^2$ and has mean $0$.

results.title: Convergence of an alternating weighted series in the plane
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be real numbers. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ let $x_k = (\alpha, \beta) \in \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$ if $k$ is even and $x_k = (\beta, \alpha)$ if $k$ is odd. For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $s_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} k^{-2} x_k$ (so $s_0 = 0$). Then the sequence $(s_n)$ converges in $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$.

results.title: Monotone functions on a closed interval with a continuous pointwise limit converge uniformly
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Monotone functions on a closed interval with a continuous pointwise limit converge uniformly. Let $a < b$ be real numbers, let $f_n : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, be nondecreasing functions, and let $g : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous with $f_n(x) \to g(x)$ for every $x \in [a, b]$. results.title: Power series agreeing at $1/2, 1/3, 1/4, \dots$ have equal coefficients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(a_k)$ and $(b_k)$ be real sequences such that the series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} a_k x^k$ and $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} b_k x^k$ converge absolutely for every real $x$ with $|x| < 1$. If $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} a_k x^k = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} b_k x^k$ for $x = 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, \dots$, then $a_k = b_k$ for all $k \ge 0$.

results.title: MPTQ set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite set $A$ of real numbers is an MPTQ (more products than quotients) set when $0 \notin A$ and $|A/A| < |A \cdot A|$, where $A \cdot A = \{ab : a, b \in A\}$ is the product set, $A/A = \{a/b : a, b \in A\}$ is the quotient set, and $|X|$ is the number of elements of $X$.

results.title: A singleton is not an MPTQ set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $a$, the one-element set $\{a\}$ is not an MPTQ set.

results.title: Sets containing zero are not MPTQ sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $A$ is a finite set of real numbers with $0 \in A$, then $A$ is not an MPTQ set.

results.title: Hegarty: no seven-element MSTD set of integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: No set of seven integers, viewed as a set of real numbers, is an MSTD set.

results.title: Hegarty's classification of MSTD sets of size eight
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a set of eight integers, regarded as a set of real numbers, and let $S = \{0, 2, 3, 4, 7, 11, 12, 14\}$. Then $A$ is an MSTD set if and only if $A = \{as + b : s \in S\}$ for some integers $a \neq 0$ and $b$.

results.title: Chu's bound for MPTQ sets of positive reals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every MPTQ set whose elements are all positive real numbers has at least $8$ elements.

results.title: Chu's bound for MPTQ sets with a negative element
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every MPTQ set of real numbers that contains a negative number has at least $5$ elements.

results.title: Adjoining an element that adds no more products than quotients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of real numbers that is not an MPTQ set, let $x$ be a real number, let $n \le m$ be natural numbers, and write $A' = A \cup \{x\}$. If $|A' \cdot A'| \le |A \cdot A| + n$ and $|A/A| + m \le |A'/A'|$, where $X \cdot X$ and $X/X$ denote the product set and quotient set of $X$, then $A'$ is not an MPTQ set.

results.title: One equal pairing of products excludes the other two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ be pairwise distinct positive real numbers with $ab = cd$. Then $ad \neq bc$ and $ac \neq bd$.

results.title: At most one square is the product of the other two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be pairwise distinct positive real numbers. Then at most one of the equations $a^2 = bc$, $b^2 = ac$ and $c^2 = ab$ holds; that is, no two of them hold simultaneously.

results.title: Five-element sets with one negative element are not MPTQ sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $A$ is a set of five real numbers exactly one of which is negative, then $A$ is not an MPTQ set.

results.title: Five-element sets with two negative elements are not MPTQ sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $A$ is a set of five real numbers exactly two of which are negative, then $A$ is not an MPTQ set.

results.title: Adjoining negatives preserves the MPTQ property
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of positive real numbers and $-A = \{-a : a \in A\}$. Then $A \cup (-A)$ is an MPTQ set if and only if $A$ is an MPTQ set.

results.title: No MPTQ set has five elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: No set of five real numbers is an MPTQ set.

results.title: Adjoining multiples by a coprime prime preserves the MPTQ property
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of integers and $p$ a prime number such that every element of $A$ is coprime to $p$, and let $pA = \{pa : a \in A\}$. Regarding sets of integers as sets of real numbers, $A \cup pA$ is an MPTQ set if and only if $A$ is an MPTQ set.

results.title: Finite simplicial sphere

results.title: Face numbers of a simplicial sphere
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite simplicial $(d-1)$-sphere $X$ and a natural number $k$, $f_k(X)$ is the number of $k$-dimensional faces of $X$, that is, of faces with exactly $k+1$ vertices.

results.title: Extended face numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite simplicial $(d-1)$-sphere $X$ and a natural number $i$, the $i$-th extended face number of $X$ is $1$ if $i = 0$, and is the number $f_{i-1}(X)$ of $(i-1)$-dimensional faces of $X$ if $i \ge 1$. Thus it equals $f_{i-1}(X)$ under the convention $f_{-1}(X) = 1$.

results.title: Dehn–Sommerville equations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a finite simplicial $(d-1)$-sphere, that is, a finite geometric simplicial complex in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose underlying space is homeomorphic to the unit sphere of $\mathbb{R}^d$. Then for every natural number $j \le d$, the h-vector of $X$ satisfies $h_j = h_{d-j}$. Here $h_j = \sum_{i=0}^{j} (-1)^{j-i} \binom{d-i}{j-i} f_{i-1}$, where $f_{-1} = 1$ and $f_k$ is the number of $k$-dimensional faces of $X$.

results.title: Two-point spin covariance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The spin covariance `Cov(σ_x, σ_y) = ⟨σ_xσ_y⟩ - ⟨σ_x⟩⟨σ_y⟩`.

results.title: Ising one-point function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The one-point function `⟨σ_x⟩`.

results.title: Covariance of a spin with a bond variable
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The covariance `⟨σ_o σ_x σ_y⟩ - ⟨σ_o⟩⟨σ_x σ_y⟩` of `σ_o` with the bond variable of `e = {x, y}`.

results.title: GHS bound for a bond
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The GHS bound `Cov(σ_o, σ_x)⟨σ_y⟩ + Cov(σ_o, σ_y)⟨σ_x⟩` for the bond `e = {x, y}`.

results.title: Bond-energy susceptibility
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The bond-energy susceptibility `∑_{e ∈ E} Cov(σ_o, σ_e)`.

results.title: Ising susceptibility at a site
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The susceptibility `χ(o) = ∑_x Cov(σ_o, σ_x)`.

results.title: GHS three-point inequality at a site for every edge
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The GHS inequality at `o` for every edge: `cov3sym ≤ ghsBoundSym`, equivalently `u₃(o, x, y) ≤ 0` for every edge `{x, y}`.

results.title: Conditional finite-volume Aizenman–Barsky–Fernández inequality
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: A conditional finite-volume form of the Aizenman–Barsky–Fernández inequality: if the GHS bound holds at `o` and the GHS bounds sum to `J ⟨σ_o⟩ χ(o)`, then the bond-energy susceptibility is at most `J ⟨σ_o⟩ χ(o)`.
